findings: The iridescent oil-slick blob in the top-right corner is the one visual risk on the page, but it is cropped and floats without a compositional counterweight on the left — the hero body sits as a plain left-aligned text column, so the relationship reads more as 'headline + decorative asset' than as a resolved composition.

Below the hero the page collapses into a single narrow centered column of running prose for nearly its entire length; the 'living art organism' promise flattens into an essay layout with no further compositional invention after the first viewport.

The four-creature specimen table and the Interference Log both use the same left-label / right-description two-column ledger pattern with faint hairline rules — reusing the same device twice in sequence blunts the editorial rhythm.

The tiny gradient chips next to Oil on water / Soap film / Morpho wing / Abalone nacre are the only chromatic events in the body and they read as swatch-library garnish rather than as compositional color.
Micro-caption tracking (ON STRUCTURAL COLOR, AN OIL SLICK IN NATURE, A SPECIMEN DRAWER) is a well-worn editorial-web trope; competent, but not a signature move.
Roman-numeral index (I–IX) with right-aligned dates is a familiar 'archive/journal' convention — executed cleanly but not reinvented.
what_works: The display serif with the italic 'angle' inside 'It is an angle of light.' is a genuine typographic decision — high-contrast editorial serif with a real voice, not system-ui slop.
The oil-slick iridescent gradient is used as a single dominant chromatic event and is not repeated across the page as garnish — restraint with color is real here.
The drop-cap 'A' in the 'morpho wing is brown' paragraph is a small but decisive editorial move a template would not ship.
The pull quote ('Tilt your head and the hue moves…') with its left rule and italic serif is set as a genuine typographic object, not a styled blockquote default.
Meta strip at the very top (ANDRE MACEDO · TELOS · ANDREMACEDO.COM · GEN 228 · EPOCH IX · STRUCTURAL COLOR) treats the header as an instrument panel rather than a nav bar — a real point of view.
A.reasoning: This is not the centered-hero-plus-three-cards template: the type is a real editorial serif with an italicized conceptual word, the hero commits to a single iridescent chromatic gesture, and the copy has a specific voice ('Color lives in the light here, not in flat fills'). Craft is visibly present in type, color restraint, and small editorial devices like the drop cap and pull quote. It falls short of an excellent score because after the hero the page settles into a long single-column essay with two near-identical ledger tables and a Roman-numeral index — competent editorial furniture, but the compositional invention of the first viewport does not sustain, and the hero itself leaves the oil-slick asset floating without a real counterweight. Above threshold, not slop, but not decisive enough to earn the high 8s.

findings: Hero text is large and asymmetric but the iridescent swirl graphic is still a soft gradient treatment
Body text blocks show uneven line-length rhythm and occasional cramped vertical gaps between sections
Specimen drawer cards use thin rules and small color swatches that read as default UI rather than expressive craft
Footer lists revert to centered two-column symmetry with date stamps that feel templated
what_works: Hero headline uses deliberate scale and italic contrast against the flowing color field
Pull-quote with purple rule creates a clear secondary focal anchor without decoration overload
B.reasoning: Desktop avoids the classic SaaS template and generic centered hero, yet spacing lacks a strict modular grid, type pairing stays safe editorial, and lower sections drift into symmetrical list formatting. Hero and restraint keep it above slop threshold but no single decisive compositional risk elevates it further.
